stemMarkdown: A 80-litre solution contains 25% acid. How many litres of water must be added to dilute it to a 10% acid solution? (Round to 2 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: The acid stays fixed at $20.00$ litres. For that to be $10\%$ of the solution, the total volume must become $\dfrac{20.00 \times 100}{10} = 200.00$ litres. Water to add $= 200.00 - 80 = 120.0$ litres.
altSolutionMarkdown: Only the solvent changes — anchoring on the unchanged solute is what makes these quick.
